g.text: VID_P primary VLAN — carries the promiscuous port, which is the uplink port; every secondary VLAN maps onto it
VID_C community VLAN — one per community; members reach each other and the promiscuous port
VID_I isolated VLAN — one per PVLAN, shared by all isolated ports, yet no isolated pair may talk
Reachability rules — the figure draws PERMITTED flows only; any pair not listed as reachable is DENIED
every port in the PVLAN, and the router beyond it
nothing — a promiscuous port is unrestricted
P1, and the router through it; ports of the SAME community
ports of any OTHER community (B1); every isolated port (I1, I2)
P1, and the router through it — nothing else
each other (I1 to I2 denied, though both sit in VID_I); A1, A2, B1
Port configuration behind the figure — every port on the switch, and its role
VID_P — the primary VLAN itself; a promiscuous port has no secondary
VID_I — one shared isolated VLAN, which is what makes the denial surprising

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology title "Private VLAN — permitted flows (figure) + the full rule set (table)"
# ── What this example is ──────────────────────────────────────────── # A worked example of `COMPLETENESS-DEFINITION` mode 3: figure PLUS table as ONE deliverable. # The figure carries the SHAPE (who is wired to whom, in which VLAN); # the tables carry the RULES — including the PROHIBITIONS, which no # arrangement of arrows can state. # # Why the split is forced here. A PVLAN figure that draws only the # permitted flows makes its most characteristic fact — "two isolated # ports cannot reach EACH OTHER even though they share VID_I" — visible # only as a MISSING edge, and absence is ambiguous: is that pair # forbidden, or merely not drawn? Meaning riding on absence is weaker # than meaning riding on presentation, and `MEANING-RECOVERY-SOURCE` rules out both. So the # closed-world reading is DECLARED, in the `reach` table caption, and # every prohibition is written out in words in its own column. # # The port count is the minimum that lets every rule be STATED rather # than gestured at: one promiscuous port, two community ports in one # community (so "same community may talk" is showable), a second # community (so "different communities may not" is showable), and two # isolated ports (so "isolated may not talk to isolated" is showable).
# ── Semantic classes: the three PVLAN VLAN types (`MEANING-RECOVERY-SOURCE`, §2.7) ──────── # Each label states a MEANING, not just a name; the legend strip below # the figure derives from these lines automatically, so an agent reads # `class=vidi` off the edge itself and never correlates hex values. class vidp "VID_P primary VLAN — carries the promiscuous port, which is the uplink port; every secondary VLAN maps onto it" stroke=#dc2626 class vidc "VID_C community VLAN — one per community; members reach each other and the promiscuous port" stroke=#2563eb class vidi "VID_I isolated VLAN — one per PVLAN, shared by all isolated ports, yet no isolated pair may talk" stroke=#16a34a style=dashed
# ── The router — beyond the switch, and not a port ────────────────── # EVERY physical port on this switch has a PVLAN role, and the uplink # port is the one configured promiscuous: P1 below IS the uplink. What # lies BEYOND that port — the router — is not a port, has no PVLAN role # and appears in no VLAN table, so it is the `external` (spec §2.8): # the edge ends open at the left margin with a label and no shape is # drawn, correctly signalling "outside this figure's scope." external rtr "Router"
# ── Port roles — four groups, six ports, one tier ──────────────────── # Every port role gets its own group so all four roles are visually # parallel: equal-weight bounded containers at the same horizontal tier. # Promiscuous is a ROLE, not a rank. P1 is a port on this switch like # the other five, configured into the primary VLAN; what distinguishes # it is unrestricted reachability, and the fact that the router happens # to hang off it. Neither makes it a parent — the router is `external`, # so no drawn shape stands above P1 for a reader to mistake for one. # The promiscuous group sits second in the stack for edge density: every # permitted flow in this figure is incident on P1, so placing it between # Community A above and Isolated below lets those edges fan both ways # over short runs. group ca "Community A — VID_C1" node ca1 "A1" in=ca node ca2 "A2" in=ca group pp "Promiscuous — VID_P" node pp1 "P1 (uplink port)" in=pp group iso "Isolated — VID_I" node ip1 "I1" in=iso node ip2 "I2" in=iso group cb "Community B — VID_C2" node cb1 "B1" in=cb
# flow right: the external sits at the left margin (outside the switch); # all four port-role groups are at the same x-tier (peers, not hierarchy). flow right
# ── Permitted reachability ────────────────────────────────────────── # Bidirectional throughout: VLAN reachability is symmetric, so a # community port that P1 can reach can also reply to P1. Every pair # NOT drawn here is denied — stated in the `reach` table, not implied # by the missing arrow. edge rtr <-> pp1 class=vidp edge pp1 <-> ca1 class=vidc edge pp1 <-> ca2 class=vidc edge pp1 <-> cb1 class=vidc edge ca1 <-> ca2 class=vidc edge pp1 <-> ip1 class=vidi edge pp1 <-> ip2 class=vidi
# ── The rules, in words ───────────────────────────────────────────── # The caption declares the closed-world reading for the whole document.
# --- panel: separate genre section (main-standard hybrid = multi-section `MULTI-FIGURE-DOCUMENTS`) --- layout # Presentation only (`GUI-WRITEBACK-STRUCTURE`: stripping these lines changes nothing semantic — # peerhood is carried by the symmetric grouping above, not by coordinates). # # The arrangement puts the two community groups side by side on the top # row, with the promiscuous port centred below them and the isolated # group at the bottom. Like sits next to like: the two communities are # the same port role, so they read as a pair. # # sizes — a two-member group holds two 150px boxes side by side; a # one-member group holds one 310px box. All four frames end up # the same size, and equal size is what carries peerhood: the # promiscuous port is a peer of the others, distinguished by # unrestricted reachability and by carrying the uplink — # neither of which is a rank. # group pins — fix the row/column slots and keep uniform clearance # between frames. Auto-layout would otherwise hoist the # external-connected pp group to the top, implying it is the # root of a hierarchy that does not exist. # member pins — group-local coordinates (spec `PIN-COORDINATE-SCOPE`). pin ca at=(190,20) pin cb at=(572,20) pin pp at=(190,146) pin iso at=(190,272) pin ca1 at=(14,20) width=150 height=44 pin ca2 at=(174,20) width=150 height=44 pin pp1 at=(14,20) width=310 height=44 pin ip1 at=(14,20) width=150 height=44 pin ip2 at=(174,20) width=150 height=44 pin cb1 at=(14,20) width=310 height=44
figdown 0.1 table table reach "Reachability rules — the figure draws PERMITTED flows only; any pair not listed as reachable is DENIED" | Port type | May reach | May NOT reach | |--------------------|------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------| | Promiscuous (P1, the uplink port) | every port in the PVLAN, and the router beyond it | nothing — a promiscuous port is unrestricted | | Community (A1, A2) | P1, and the router through it; ports of the SAME community | ports of any OTHER community (B1); every isolated port (I1, I2) | | Isolated (I1, I2) | P1, and the router through it — nothing else | each other (I1 to I2 denied, though both sit in VID_I); A1, A2, B1| cell 3 highlight
table ports "Port configuration behind the figure — every port on the switch, and its role" | Port | Port type | VLAN membership | |---------------|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------| | P1 (uplink) | promiscuous | VID_P — the primary VLAN itself; a promiscuous port has no secondary | | A1, A2 | community | VID_C1 | | B1 | community | VID_C2 | | I1, I2 | isolated | VID_I — one shared isolated VLAN, which is what makes the denial surprising |
